analysis.title: Fed in the spotlight in a busier week
key_insights: CA-CIB leans toward a Fed skip at the October FOMC (decision Wed 28 Oct, upper bound held at 4.00%), followed by another 25bp hike in December. The decision has become a closer call after upside surprises in September CPI and PPI.

Williams, Jefferson and Waller have hinted at a preference to hold in October. Waller said the Fed will likely need to hike more but has flexibility on timing, since hikes do not need to come at consecutive meetings. CA-CIB reads this group as biased toward holding and says the inflation data does not quite reach the bar to change that.

CA-CIB expects September core PCE up about 0.33% MoM, so rounding to 0.4% cannot be ruled out, with YoY edging up to 3.1% from 3.0%. Headline PCE is expected up 0.5% MoM, taking YoY to 3.6% from 3.4%. This keeps further hikes such as December on the table.

Personal income is expected up 0.2% MoM and personal spending up 0.5% MoM, so real spending would be soft given the PCE deflator. This follows a very strong August (spending +0.9%), and consumption is on track for another solid quarter in the 3% range.

Q3 advance GDP is expected at 3.0% QoQ SAAR versus 2.2% in Q2 2026, driven by strong consumption and robust non-residential investment. This would show the economy staying resilient despite the ongoing war in Iran.

Durable goods orders for September are expected to rise strongly on a surge in Boeing orders (CA-CIB cites 1.8% versus -0.1% in August), though the headline is noisy. Consumer confidence is expected to weaken (82.5 versus 81.9 prior is the calendar figure) and new home sales to come in softer (653k versus 684k).

CA-CIB forecasts 2026 US growth of 2.3% (cut from 2.5% because of the Iran war) and 2.1% in 2027, with fiscal support from the Big Beautiful Bill and a diminishing trade-policy drag as offsets. Unemployment is seen stabilizing in the low-4% range, with the 4.5% November 2025 print as the peak.

CA-CIB has headline CPI peaking at 4.2% YoY in May 2026 and staying above 3.0% into early 2027 before dropping to the low 2.0% range from Q2 2027. Core CPI is forecast between about 2.4% and 2.7% YoY through early 2027 and about 2.3% by end-2027.

The Fed hiked in September. CA-CIB expects two more 25bp hikes in December and March to take the upper bound back to 4.50%, with consecutive hikes a risk. It then projects two 25bp cuts in Q4 2027 to take the upper bound to 4.00%.
Employment cost index (Q3) is due Friday 30 October with no CA-CIB forecast, against 0.9% in Q2. The October jobs report is due 6 November and October CPI on 12 November.

risk_factors: Inflation stickiness, especially in PCE, and the energy spike from the Iran war add upside risk to inflation forecasts.
Consecutive Fed hikes are a risk to CA-CIB's base case of a skip in October.
The concentrated, K-shaped nature of recent growth.
AI replacing job functions could weigh on the labor market.
CA-CIB wrote the report on 16 October and may change forecasts after data released in the interim.
geopolitical: The ongoing war in Iran is a drag on 2026 US growth (forecast cut to 2.3% from 2.5%) and drives the energy spike lifting headline inflation.

tension_points.bull_case: The hawkish side sees firm CPI and PPI in September and a firm PCE print as grounds to hike in October. CA-CIB itself thinks consecutive hikes would be the better approach for the Fed.
tension_points.bear_case: Williams, Jefferson and Waller have hinted at a preference to hold in October to gather more information. Waller said hikes do not need to come at consecutive meetings, and the inflation data does not quite reach the bar for the broader committee.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A hotter-than-expected September PCE would add pressure toward hiking, though it prints the day after the meeting. CA-CIB will publish a final call in its Fed preview on Monday.

theme_stances.key_argument: The inflation data does not quite reach the bar for the broader committee to agree on an October hike, but it keeps additional hikes on the table later such as in December.
theme_stances.evidence: we continue to lean towards a skip in October followed by another hike in December
